ledger.note: 1576: the first dated event on the pages (the siege of Takabaru, 'a battle he won', Yoshihisa page). The clan has held Satsuma since 1186 and 'subdued Hyūga and Ōsumi' in 1196 (clan page); the dossier opens at 1576, bridged, confidence 1.

region.text: the northern half of Hyūga, held in part by the Ōtomo

ledger.note: 10 December 1578: Mimigawa on the Mimi River in Hyūga, a Shimazu victory; Toshihisa pursued survivors to the Ōtomo headquarters at Matsuyama castle. The pages give no territorial result ('did not take their territory', Yoshihisa page); the Ōtomo held half of Hyūga (Ōtomo clan page) and the Shimazu held 'Hyūga' by mid-1585, so the gain is bridged to 1578, confidence 1.

1581: 'His forces took Minamata castle in Higo Province with 115,000 men'; the Aso clan was defeated in early 1584. The Higo holders are not named on the page; the extent of the holding is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Hizen Province: Saga and Nagasaki Prefectures

ledger.note: 3 May 1584: Okitanawate near Shimabara in Hizen, the combined Shimazu and Arima forces against the Ryūzōji; Ryūzōji Takanobu killed, 10,000 Ryūzōji dead. The Okitanawate page does not say who held Hizen afterwards; the Yoshihisa page lists Hizen as Shimazu by mid-1585.

1585: Horikiri Castle in Chikugo attacked and Iwaya Castle taken after the invasion of Chikuzen; by mid-1585 the Shimazu controlled both. The Ōtomo clan page holds both provinces among the Ōtomo's six; the page does not name the defenders.

1586: the Shimazu 'seized Funai Castle from the Ōtomo'; 'Bungo province fell to them' after Hetsugigawa (Kyūshū campaign page). The Yoshihisa page does not say they took Bungo in 1586 and lists Bungo as the Ōtomo's in mid-1585.

sources.title: Shimazu clan
sources.note: 1186 Tadahisa shugo of Satsuma; 1196 subdued Hyuga and Osumi; home provinces Satsuma, Osumi, Hyuga; 1586 Yoshihisa unified and controlled the entire Kyushu region; 1587 retired after Hideyoshi's Kyushu campaign; 1601 Iehisa first Lord of Satsuma; 1609 Ryukyu; Yoshihiro daimyo at Sekigahara.

sources.title: Shimazu Yoshihisa
sources.note: 1576 Takabaru; 1578 Mimigawa; 1581 Minamata in Higo; early 1584 Okitanawate in Hizen against the Ryuzoji, the Aso defeated; 1585 Horikiri in Chikugo, Iwaya in Chikuzen; mid-1585 Chikugo, Chikuzen, Hizen, Higo, Hyuga, Osumi and Satsuma controlled, Otomo the exception; 1586 Tachibana; June 1587 routed in Satsuma; 1587 settlement, the Shimazu kept Satsuma, Osumi and half of Hyuga.

sources.title: Kyūshū campaign
sources.note: 1586 Shimazu lifted the Tachibana siege and seized Funai from the Otomo; Bungo fell to them after Hetsugigawa; 1587 Hidenaga at Takajo in Hyuga, the Shimazu forced back to Satsuma; they surrendered later in 1587, Kagoshima not attacked.

sources.title: Battle of Mimigawa
sources.note: 10 December 1578 on the Mimi River in Hyuga; Shimazu victory over the Otomo; Toshihisa pursued survivors to the Otomo headquarters at Matsuyama castle; no territorial consequence on the page.

sources.title: Battle of Okitanawate
sources.note: 3 May 1584 near Shimabara, Hizen; Shimazu and Arima forces against the Ryuzoji; Ryuzoji Takanobu killed; allied victory.

sources.title: Ōtomo clan
sources.note: Bungo and Buzen shugo from 1185; at its height six provinces (Buzen, Bungo, Hizen, Higo, Chikuzen, Chikugo) and two half-provinces (Hyuga and Iyo).

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from six pages (Shimazu clan, Shimazu Yoshihisa, Kyūshū campaign, Battle of Mimigawa, Battle of Okitanawate, Ōtomo clan). A Sengoku daimyo domain inside Cliopatria's single Warring States Japan row. The dossier opens at 1576 (first dated event on the pages) and closes at 1600; the Shimazu rule of Satsuma from 1186 and the 1196 subjugation of Hyūga and Ōsumi (clan page) are not dated enough to draw before 1576. Drawn from the pages: Hyūga north (bridged 1578), Higo (1581), Hizen (1584), Chikuzen and Chikugo (1585), Bungo (1586), then the 1587 settlement. Page conflicts: the clan page says that in 1586 Yoshihisa 'succeeded in unifying and controlling the entire Kyushu region' while the Yoshihisa page has mid-1585 control of seven provinces, 'leaving Ōtomo's domain as the main exception', and does not say Bungo fell in 1586; the Kyūshū campaign page has Bungo fall after Hetsugigawa in 1586. The Yoshihisa page's own dates conflict (birth 1533 or 1535, death March or January 1611); not used. Not on the pages: Buzen, Tsukushi and the Aso lands, the Itō clan of Hyūga, the 1587 submission wording (the clan page says 'retired', not 'submitted'), Korea (the Shimazu fought there; the page is silent), Sekigahara (the clan page names Yoshihiro but gives no year). Counterpart strings: 'toyotomi-clan', 'satsuma-domain' and 'otomo-clan' exist; the others are clans named on the pages. Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
